- [USER] User expressed interest in comparing horror styles of classic authors like Poe and Lovecraft with contemporary writers such as Shirley Jackson and Stephen Graham Jones.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Classic horror authors such as Poe and Lovecraft often relied on supernatural elements to create fear and horror in their readers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Classic horror writers used gothic settings, mysterious creatures, and otherworldly beings to build tension and terror.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Classic horror writing focused on the unknown and the fear that comes with encountering the unknown.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Contemporary horror writers such as Shirley Jackson and Stephen Graham Jones tend to focus more on psychological horror.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Contemporary horror delves into the human psyche, exploring what drives people to do evil things.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Contemporary horror is grounded in reality, exploring fears encountered in daily life like fear of death, fear of the unknown, and fear of losing control.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both classic and contemporary horror writers aim to create a sense of unease and fear in their readers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The ultimate goal of both classic and contemporary horror writers is to keep their readers on the edge of their seats, unable to look away.
